articles.title: Foreign Investors Are Quietly Shifting to Short-Term Indian Bonds. The Signal Is Hard to Ignore.
articles.excerpt: Two-thirds of top foreign bond purchases in March through May were in maturities under five years. The front end of the curve now offers better risk-adjusted carry — and the back end is a bet most fund managers do not want to take.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, where the MPC will announce its rate decision on Friday
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Trade Deal With Britain Is Stuck on Steel. Scotch Whisky Is Being Used as Leverage.
articles.excerpt: Britain's new steel safeguards cut tariff-free imports by 60 per cent. India is now reviewing the duty concessions it offered on whisky, automobiles and medical devices as a countermeasure.
articles.image_caption: UK Trade Minister Peter Kyle after returning from trade talks in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Just Proposed a 12.5% Tariff on India Over Forced Labour. Sixty Countries Are in the Crosshairs.
articles.excerpt: The Section 301 investigation is designed to rebuild the tariff architecture the Supreme Court dismantled in February. India rejected the allegations and said it would seek resolution through trade talks.
articles.image_caption: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced the proposed tariffs under Section 301
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rubio Told Congress That India Is Central to American Foreign Policy. He Was Not Exaggerating.
articles.excerpt: In a marathon Congressional testimony, the Secretary of State cited India more than any other partner — on trade, the Quad, de-escalation with Pakistan, and the Indo-Pacific strategy that now anchors Washington's Asia doctrine.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who cited India as central to American foreign policy during Congressional testimony
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New Grid Rules Could Cut Solar Revenues by 11% and Wind by 48%. The Investors Are Already Walking.
articles.excerpt: KKR, Canada Pension Plan, Actis, and Macquarie-backed Blueleaf have warned Indian officials that tighter power grid penalties are advancing faster than the infrastructure to support them.
articles.image_caption: A solar energy installation in India, part of the country's push toward 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New Trade Pact With Oman Bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. That May Matter More Than the Tariff Cuts.
articles.excerpt: The India-Oman CEPA grants duty-free access to 99% of Indian exports — but the agreement's real strategic value lies in Oman's coastline, which sits outside the world's most dangerous chokepoint.
articles.image_caption: The Port of Salalah in Oman, located outside the Strait of Hormuz on the Arabian Sea coastline
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Launched Its First Mass-Market Ethanol Motorcycles. The Price Difference Is Less Than a Tank of Petrol.
articles.excerpt: Hero MotoCorp's Splendor+ and HF Deluxe can now run on E85. With India importing 87% of its fossil fuel, the ₹172 premium on the cheapest model is a rounding error.
articles.image_caption: Hero MotoCorp's Splendor and HF Deluxe are India's best-selling motorcycle families
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Farmer's Daughter Died Because India's Biggest Medical Exam Was Cancelled. She Was Not the Last Victim.
articles.excerpt: Akanksha Chaturvedi scored well on NEET. Then the paper leak happened. The re-exam broke her. Now scammers are selling fake papers to desperate families for ₹20 lakh.
articles.image_caption: NEET aspirants face an uncertain future after the cancellation of the May 3 examination
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Just Agreed to Hand Over Its India Financials to the Antitrust Regulator. It Had Refused for Years.
articles.excerpt: The CCI found Apple abused its dominant position in 2024. Apple fought the case and withheld its books. A Delhi judge told the company to cooperate. Now it has.
articles.image_caption: Apple's iPhone market share in India has grown from 2 percent to 9 percent in five years
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Will Announce Its Rate Decision Tomorrow. It May Be the Hardest Call Sanjay Malhotra Has Ever Made.
articles.excerpt: With the rupee at record lows, crude oil near $96, and inflation still below target, India's central bank faces a policy dilemma that has no clean answer.
articles.image_caption: India's central bank faces a critical rate decision amid economic uncertainty
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is About to Place Its Largest-Ever Military Drone Order. The $2 Billion Will Go Entirely to Domestic Firms.
articles.excerpt: Lessons from the Pakistan confrontation and the Iran war have fast-tracked India's biggest unmanned systems purchase. Deliveries are expected within 18 to 24 months.
articles.image_caption: An Indian military unmanned aerial vehicle during a defence exercise
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Supreme Court Just Called Every Mobile Phone a 'Virtual Gambling House.' The Online Gaming Industry Is Reeling.
articles.excerpt: The court upheld state bans on online betting — even on games of skill — and backed 28% GST on the full value of bets. Dream11, MPL and 27 other companies face an existential reckoning.
articles.image_caption: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi's Five-Nation Tour Is Not Ceremonial Diplomacy. It Is a Supply-Chain Emergency.
articles.excerpt: With Hormuz choked, crude at $97 and the rupee near record lows, India's prime minister is racing through the UAE and four European capitals to lock down energy, tech and trade alternatives.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, whose five-nation diplomatic tour this week reflects India's urgent push to secure energy and trade partnerships
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SEBI Just Accused India's Biggest Gold Refiner of Fabricating $158 Billion in Revenue. The Numbers Were Never Real.
articles.excerpt: Rajesh Exports and its chairman have been barred from the securities market after the regulator found that 99.8 per cent of the company's consolidated revenue came from subsidiaries whose books could not be verified.
articles.image_caption: Rajesh Exports, headquartered in Bengaluru, is known as the world's largest gold processor by volume
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is About to Offer ₹3,000 Crore to Build Its Own Lithium and Nickel Processing Industry. The EV Race Demands It.
articles.excerpt: The Ministry of Mines will shortly unveil an incentive policy for processing lithium and nickel domestically, with minimum capacity thresholds designed to attract industrial-scale operations.
articles.image_caption: India aims to build domestic lithium and nickel processing capacity to secure its electric vehicle supply chain
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Worker Was Killed When Iranian Drones Hit Kuwait's Airport. The Gulf Is No Longer Safe Ground for the Diaspora.
articles.excerpt: India condemned the attack and said its embassy was assisting the family, as Kuwait expelled two Iranian diplomats and the airport resumed flights from a backup terminal after severe damage to Terminal 1.
articles.image_caption: Kuwait International Airport's Terminal 1 sustained severe damage in the Iranian drone and missile attack on June 3, 2026
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Global Companies Are Using India's IPO Market as an Exit Door. The Rupee Is Paying the Price.
articles.excerpt: From Hyundai to Walmart's PhonePe, foreign firms are listing in India not to raise capital but to cash out — and the $23 billion in outflows this year shows the cost.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Fire in a Bihar Hospital's ICU Killed at Least Four People. The Staff Had Already Fled.
articles.excerpt: A short circuit at Prasad Hospital in Muzaffarpur turned the intensive care unit into a death trap. Families say doctors abandoned patients as smoke filled the building.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Scraps Capital Gains Tax on Foreign Investment in Government Bonds. The Rupee Forced Its Hand.
articles.excerpt: The cabinet approved an ordinance eliminating the 12.5% long-term capital gains tax and possibly the 20% withholding tax on interest — a dramatic bid to lure back foreign capital as the rupee hits record lows.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Fined PhysicsWallah for Sneaking a ₹10 Donation Into Every Checkout. McAfee Got Caught Too.
articles.excerpt: The consumer watchdog penalised both companies for dark patterns — auto-added charges, guilt-tripping cancellation screens, and data harvesting disguised as free courses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York's Senate Just Voted to Recognise India's Independence Day. The Man Behind It Was Adopted From Kolkata.
articles.excerpt: Resolution J1935 urges the governor to proclaim August 15, 2026, as India Independence Day across New York State. The sponsor, Jeremy Cooney, is the first Asian American elected to state office from upstate New York.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Froze EB-2 Visas for Indians. The Backlog Now Stretches Back to 2014.
articles.excerpt: All employment-based second-preference visas for Indian nationals have been exhausted for FY 2026. Processing will not resume until October.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Commerce Minister Says the US Trade Deal Is '99% Done.' The Last 1% Is the Hard Part.
articles.excerpt: As American negotiators wrap up four days of talks in New Delhi, a new 12.5% tariff threat under Section 301 complicates what was supposed to be a triumphant finish.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Venezuela's Acting President Just Landed in Delhi. India's Oil Crisis Brought Her Here.
articles.excerpt: Delcy Rodriguez's five-day visit coincides with India importing 427,000 barrels a day of Venezuelan crude — the most since 2020 — as the Hormuz blockade forces New Delhi to look west.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US House Just Voted to End the Iran War. Four Republicans Made It Happen.
articles.excerpt: The 215-208 vote is the clearest Congressional rebuke of Trump's three-month-old conflict, but the measure still faces a Senate gauntlet and a certain veto.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Fire in a Delhi Hotel Killed 21 People, Most of Them Foreign Nationals Who Came for Medical Treatment.
articles.excerpt: The Flourish Stay B&B in Malviya Nagar operated 25 rooms on a licence that allowed six. The owner is on the run, and the building had no fire safety clearance.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 58 Rebel MLAs Just Broke Away From Mamata Banerjee's Party. The TMC Has Never Faced a Crisis Like This.
articles.excerpt: Expelled leaders Ritabrata Banerjee and Sandipan Saha claim the Speaker has recognised their faction as the official opposition. The party dissolved all its committees in response. Mamata blames the BJP and police for engineering the split.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russia's Biggest Bank Just Asked India to Send More Workers. Moscow's Construction Sites Cannot Function Without Them.
articles.excerpt: Sberbank called for simplified immigration at the St. Petersburg Economic Forum. Indian work permits in Russia jumped from 5,000 to 72,000 in four years, and the country still needs 789,000 more construction workers by 2030.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Just Confirmed He Called Netanyahu 'Crazy.' The Ceasefire India Needs Is Nowhere Close.
articles.excerpt: The leaked phone call, the stalled talks with Iran, and the overnight strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain reveal a war that is fracturing the alliances meant to end it. India, with 9 million workers in the Gulf, has no good options.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Will Surpass Nehru on June 10 to Become India's Longest-Serving Elected Prime Minister.
articles.excerpt: After 4,399 consecutive days in office, the man from Vadnagar will hold a record that has stood since 1964. The country he governs looks nothing like the one Nehru left behind.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Supreme Court Just Drew a Line Between Sex Work and Trafficking. The Distinction Changes Everything.
articles.excerpt: In a landmark ruling, Justices Pardiwala and Mahadevan held that adult women who choose sex work cannot be arrested, harassed or forcibly rehabilitated. The 70-year-old law stays. The way it is enforced does not.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Britain's Foreign Secretary Arrives in India for the First Time. The Agenda Goes Far Beyond Trade.
articles.excerpt: Yvette Cooper will meet Jaishankar and Modi on Thursday. The UK-India Vision 2035 review, the Iran war and the Free Trade Agreement are all on the table — but maritime security may be the most urgent item.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi's Cabinet Just Approved a ₹39,290 Crore Stimulus. The Biggest Item Is a Bet on Cheaper Jet Fuel.
articles.excerpt: A ₹10,000 crore Aviation Turbine Fuel stabilisation fund, a ₹5,041 crore Delhi transport overhaul and over ₹24,000 crore in new highways — the package is designed to absorb the economic shock of the Iran war.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Proposed Killing 'Duration of Status' for Student Visas. Indian Graduates Have the Most to Lose.
articles.excerpt: A new DHS rule would replace open-ended student stays with a fixed four-year limit and shut down the Day 1 CPT workaround that thousands of Indians rely on after losing the H-1B lottery.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Services Sector Just Had Its Best Month Since November. The Jobs Data Tells a Different Story.
articles.excerpt: HSBC's India Services PMI rose to 59.8 in May, the highest in six months, on a surge in domestic demand. But fewer than 7 percent of firms are actually hiring.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Quietly Interrogating Companies That Sent Money Abroad. The Rupee Crisis Made It Inevitable.
articles.excerpt: The RBI and SEBI have sent at least 10 queries in three weeks to firms and family offices routing money overseas. The $250,000 LRS window is next.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Proposed a 12.5% Tariff on India Over Forced Labour. Trade Talks in Delhi Are Still Going.
articles.excerpt: Washington's Section 301 investigation names India among 54 economies without a forced-labour import ban. The timing — mid-negotiation — is not a coincidence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Over 200,000 H-1B Applicants Paid $100,000 Each This Year. Most of Them Are Likely Indian.
articles.excerpt: DHS Secretary Mullin told the Senate that 70 percent of this year's H-1B applicants opted for expedited processing at the cost introduced by Trump's 2025 proclamation.

sources.label: US Chamber of Commerce court filing

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The OECD Just Said What Everyone Feared. A Long War Could Trigger the Worst Slowdown Since the Pandemic.
articles.excerpt: If the Middle East conflict drags into 2027, global growth could fall to 2.1 percent — with Asia, and India in particular, bearing the heaviest burden.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CMR Green's IPO Was Fully Subscribed in a Single Day. It Is India's First Mainboard Issue in a Month.
articles.excerpt: The ₹630 crore offering from a Faridabad metal recycler drew 2x oversubscription from non-institutional investors. The primary market had been frozen since early May.
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Indian markets have watched the primary market freeze since early May. CMR Green's day-one oversubscription signals that retail and institutional appetite may be returning despite the Iran war's market turbulence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Annamalai Met Amit Shah for 30 Minutes. The BJP Still Says He Has Not Resigned.
articles.excerpt: The former Tamil Nadu BJP president is expected to announce a new political movement after his birthday on June 4. The party is making a last effort to keep him.
articles.nri_angle: Annamalai has a significant following among Tamil NRIs in the Bay Area, Singapore and the UK. A new party with his personal brand could tap into diaspora fundraising networks that currently flow to national parties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Monsoon Is Late, Weak and Facing El Niño. The Kharif Season Is Already Behind.
articles.excerpt: The IMD now expects onset over Kerala on June 4 — nine days past its original forecast. Day one of the season saw 55% below-normal rainfall across the country.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with family in farming communities across India face rising food prices if the monsoon underperforms. A weak season would compound the inflation already driven by the Iran war's oil shock, hitting remittance purchasing power.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iranian Drones Hit Kuwait's Airport, Killing One and Shutting Down Flights Two Days After It Reopened.
articles.excerpt: The attack on Terminal 1 is the most significant strike on a civilian facility since the April ceasefire. An estimated one million Indian nationals in Kuwait are caught in the crossfire.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Says It Did Not Sell $12 Billion in Gold. Bloomberg's Data Says Otherwise.
articles.excerpt: India's central bank issued an unusually blunt denial after a Bloomberg Economics analysis suggested it had liquidated gold reserves to defend the rupee. The weekly data tells a more complicated story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DK Shivakumar Takes Oath as Karnataka Chief Minister. It Took Four Decades to Get Here.
articles.excerpt: The Congress veteran known as the 'Rock of Kanakapura' was sworn in at Bengaluru's Lok Bhavan, backed by the party's full national leadership and a cabinet that will form in stages.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Myanmar's President Just Promised Modi That Indian Insurgents Will Not Use Its Territory. It Is the Strongest Guarantee in Years.
articles.excerpt: The summit at Hyderabad House covered border security, fencing, Aung San Suu Kyi, and an expanding agenda from trade to space cooperation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Issued a ₹3.25 Lakh Crore Order for 114 Rafale Jets. It Is the Largest Defence Deal in Indian History.
articles.excerpt: Of the 114 jets, 94 will be manufactured in India by Dassault Aviation — the biggest Make in India defence programme ever launched.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Economy Likely Grew 7.2% Last Quarter. It Is Still the Fastest-Growing Major Economy on Earth.
articles.excerpt: A Reuters poll of 45 economists expects GDP growth eased from 7.8% in October-December. The data, due Friday, will be the first real measure of how tariffs and the Iran war have begun to bite.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs tracking India's economic trajectory, the 7.2% number is impressive by any global standard — China managed 4.7% and the US 2.3% over the same period. But a growth model dependent on government spending while private investment stays muted is one that sustains momentum for quarters, not decades. The sectors that employ diaspora talent — technology, pharmaceuticals, financial services — face specific headwinds the aggregate number obscures.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Inc. Just Beat Earnings Estimates for the Quarter. The Iran War May Erase the Gains.
articles.excerpt: Nifty 50 companies posted 6.6% profit growth in the January-March quarter, well ahead of the 2% forecast. Mid-caps grew 35%. But elevated oil at $97 and a record foreign fund exodus threaten the quarters ahead.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI investors with Indian market exposure through direct equities, mutual funds, or India-focused ETFs, the Q4 numbers confirm the domestic consumption story. But the IT sector's tepid revenue growth is relevant for diaspora tech workers who hold stock in Indian IT companies. The AI disruption narrative cuts both ways — threatening legacy outsourcing but potentially driving new demand for AI services.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Maersk Just Launched a New Shipping Route From Shanghai to Gujarat. India's Trade Deficit With China Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: The FI2 service deploys six container ships carrying 4,500 TEU each. Pipavav port's rail link to Delhi makes this more than a shipping route — it is a supply chain shortcut for India's biggest trade partner.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI entrepreneurs and import-export businesses with India operations, the new route reduces transit times for Chinese components that power everything from electronics assembly to EV manufacturing. E-commerce platforms like Amazon and Flipkart will benefit from faster restocking, which matters for diaspora-funded D2C brands selling through these marketplaces.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
